name: UUID in its standard textual form
description: A 128-bit UUID written in the standard hex-and-dash textual form (8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits). The legacy Heroku API key family is documented as a bare UUID of this form, so the two share a shape. The UUID specification states that UUIDs are not to be assumed hard to guess and must not be used as security capabilities; it does not say that any particular UUID-shaped value is or is not a secret, so the shape alone settles neither reading and the sibling asserts nothing about a given value. Ordinary UUID-shaped identifiers (request, release, application, project ids) are the common benign case.

sources.supports: The hex-and-dash textual form of a UUID (4hexOctet-2hexOctet-2hexOctet-2hexOctet-6hexOctet), which is the 8-4-4-4-12 shape.
Implementations SHOULD NOT assume UUIDs are hard to guess and MUST NOT use them as security capabilities (identifiers whose mere possession grants access).
